mainTopic: Liability of bandits and shepherds for an animal's damage, רבא's rule about a שומר who hands over to another שומר, and whether a שומר אבידה is a paid or unpaid guard
overview: The גמרא first asks why the משנה needs to say that לסטים who took an animal out are liable, since that seems obvious. It answers that they only stood in front of the animal and drove it out, like רב's ruling about someone who 'stands' an animal near another person's grain. אביי adds that this means they hit the animal with a stick. Next the גמרא asks whose place the shepherd in the משנה takes, and concludes that he replaces the שומר, not the owner. That seems to contradict רבא, who says a שומר who hands over to another שומר stays liable. The גמרא answers for רבא that the משנה means a shepherd passing the animal to his own helper. In a second version, the משנה's wording seems to support רבא, but that proof is rejected. Then רבה and רב יוסף argue whether a שומר אבידה is like a שומר חנם or a שומר שכר, and the גמרא gives the reasons for each side. After a memory list, רב יוסף begins a challenge against רבה that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why say the bandits are liable? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that לסטים who took the animal out are liable, calling it obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious! Once the bandits took the animal out, it is in their possession for everything, including damage it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is questioning why the משנה bothered to teach that לסטים who took an animal out of the pen must pay for its damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bandits removed the animal, they have taken control of it, so naturally they are responsible for whatever it does. A ruling that obvious seems to teach nothing new, so the גמרא asks what the משנה is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why does this need to be said?

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'פשיטא' does not mean the גמרא disagrees with the ruling. It agrees, but wants to know why it needed to be said.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
phrases.notes: This is about the משנה's line that when bandits take the animal out, the bandits are the ones who pay.

phrases.english: Since they took it out,
it stands in their possession for all matters!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to the משנה's ruling about לסטים
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that לסטים who removed the animal are liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking the animal out puts it fully in their control, so their liability is self-evident and needs no teaching

steps.title: The case is where the bandits only stood in front of it
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed for a case where the לסטים did not lead the animal out but stood before it and drove it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the ruling is needed where they stood in front of the animal and drove it out, without leading it by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a less obvious case: the bandits never took hold of the animal. They only stood in front of it so that it went out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that someone who never touched or led the animal has not taken it into his possession and so is not liable. The משנה teaches that even this indirect driving makes the לסטים responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (a less obvious case)
They stood in front of it

phrases.english: No, it is necessary where they stood in front of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge by narrowing the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the bandits did not physically take the animal, they would not be liable
steps.terutzMaskana: Even driving the animal out from in front makes the לסטים liable

steps.title: A parallel ruling of רב about standing an animal near grain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares this to רב's ruling that one who 'stands' another's animal near a third person's grain is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רבה said in the name of רב מתנה, who said it in the name of רב: one who stands his friend's animal near another person's standing grain is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a similar ruling from רב to show that this kind of indirect action already counts as making someone liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב's case, a person brings someone else's animal to a third person's field, and the animal eats the grain. The person who placed it there pays, even though the animal is not his. This sets up the next question about why רב needed to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: One who stands (places) an animal somewhere
Standing grain, crops still growing in the field

phrases.english: Like this that Rabba said
that Rav Mattana said that Rav said:
One who stands his fellow's animal
near his fellow's standing grain is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel case to support the answer
steps.raayaObject: That driving an animal from in front creates liability
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling about המעמיד בהמת חברו על קמת חבירו

steps.title: Placing the animal there: isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב needed to say that one who places the animal at the grain is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stood the animal there, it is obvious that he is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same 'obvious' question about רב's ruling that it asked about the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone actively places an animal next to grain, he clearly caused the damage. So what is רב teaching?

phrases.english: He stands it there? That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the parallel ruling just quoted
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that המעמיד is liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone who actively places the animal at the grain is obviously responsible

steps.title: רב also means standing in front of the animal
steps.stepSummary: רב's case is also one where the person only stood in front of the animal and drove it toward the grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where he stood in front of the animal and drove it toward the grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer for רב as it gave for the משנה. The person did not lead the animal; he only drove it from in front.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the two cases really match. Both the לסטים and the person in רב's case acted only indirectly, and both are still liable.
steps.whatToRemember: Both the משנה's לסטים and רב's מעמיד are liable even when they did not lead the animal by hand but drove it from in front.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary where he stood in front of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge on רב in the same way as step 2
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without leading the animal, one is not responsible for what it eats
steps.terutzMaskana: Driving it from in front is enough for liability

steps.title: אביי: the bandits also hit the animal
steps.stepSummary: אביי reminds רב יוסף that he explained רב's case as hitting the animal, and says the לסטים case must also mean they hit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: You told us that רב's case means he hit the animal. So the bandits too must be a case where they hit it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי makes 'standing in front of it' more precise. It is not just standing there; it means hitting the animal with a stick, and this applies to the bandits too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף had explained רב's ruling as a case of hitting the animal. Since the גמרא compared the לסטים to רב's case, אביי says the לסטים case should be read the same way. Liability comes from striking the animal and driving it, not from merely standing nearby.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
'He hit it,' you told us,
phrases.notes: רב יוסף had explained רב's 'standing in front of it' as hitting the animal with a stick.

phrases.english: so the bandits too are a case where they hit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף: הִכִּישָׁהּ אֲמַרְתְּ לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines the answer by defining 'standing in front' as hitting
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Merely standing in front of the animal might be enough
steps.terutzMaskana: Both cases are where the animal was hit and driven

steps.title: The shepherd takes whose place?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about giving the animal to a shepherd and asks whose place the shepherd takes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if he gave it to a shepherd, the shepherd takes his place. They asked: in place of whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. It asks who exactly the shepherd replaces in responsibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just says 'in his place' without saying whose place. The question sets up a test of two possible readings.

phrases.english: If he handed it to a shepherd,
the shepherd enters, etc.
They said: in place of whom?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסָרָהּ לְרוֹעֶה – נִכְנַס הָרוֹעֶה כּוּ׳. אָמְרִי: תַּחְתָּיו דְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on the next line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whom does the shepherd replace in responsibility

steps.title: Not the owner, since that was already taught
steps.stepSummary: The shepherd cannot mean 'in place of the owner', because an earlier משנה already taught that every kind of שומר takes the owner's place.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means in place of the animal's owner, we already learned once: if he handed it to an unpaid guard, a borrower, a paid guard, or a renter, they all take the owner's place!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, that the shepherd replaces the owner, and rejects it because it would repeat an earlier משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier משנה already listed שומר חנם, שואל, נושא שכר and שוכר as taking over from the owner. Repeating this for a shepherd would teach nothing new, so that cannot be the meaning.

phrases.english: If you say in place of the animal's owner,
we already learned it once:
phrases.notes: This is an earlier משנה in this מסכת (44b).

phrases.english: If he handed it to an unpaid guard, or to a borrower,
to a paid guard, or to a renter,
they all enter in place of the owner!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא תַּחְתָּיו דְּבַעַל בְּהֵמָה – תְּנֵינָא חֲדָא זִמְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'in his place' as 'in place of the owner'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That would just repeat a rule already taught in an earlier משנה

steps.title: The shepherd takes the guard's place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the shepherd replaces the שומר who handed the animal over to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means in place of the guard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer: the משנה is talking about a שומר who passed the animal on to a shepherd, and now the shepherd takes over the guard's responsibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reading teaches something new. A שומר who hands the animal to a shepherd is no longer liable for its damage, because the shepherd now stands in his place.
steps.whatToRemember: The shepherd in the משנה replaces the שומר, not the owner, because the owner case was already taught in an earlier משנה.

phrases.english: Rather, in place of the guard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second reading after the first was rejected
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The shepherd takes the place of the שומר who handed him the animal

steps.title: Is the first guardian completely free? A challenge to רבא
steps.stepSummary: If the shepherd fully replaces the first שומר, then the first שומר is off the hook. That seems to contradict רבא, who says a שומר who hands over to another שומר stays liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is the first guardian completely exempt? Shall we say this is a refutation of רבא, who said: a guardian who handed over to another guardian is liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from step 9 and uses it to attack רבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said the shepherd takes the place of the first שומר. That suggests the first שומר is free of all responsibility. But רבא rules that a שומר who passes the item to another שומר remains liable, so the משנה seems to disprove him.

keyTerms.meaning: The first guardian, the one who originally received the animal
A refutation; a strong challenge from a source that seems to disprove someone
A guardian who handed the item over to another guardian

phrases.english: And the first guardian
is completely exempt?
Shall we say this is a refutation of רבא?
For רבא said:
A guardian who handed over to another guardian is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what step 9's answer implies and uses it against רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a שומר who hands over to another שומר is liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה has the shepherd fully replace the first שומר, so the first שומר seems exempt. That clashes with רבא, who keeps him liable.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה means a shepherd handing the animal to his helper
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers on רבא's behalf: the משנה is about a shepherd who gave the animal to his own helper. That is normal, so it is not the case of handing over to an outside שומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא can tell you: what does 'he gave it to a shepherd' mean? To his helper, since it is a shepherd's normal way to hand animals to his helper.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא's ruling on his behalf by reading the משנה as a special, normal case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An owner who gives an animal to a shepherd knows the shepherd's helper will also handle it. So passing it to the helper is expected, and the shepherd is not at fault. רבא's rule only covers handing the item to an outside person, so the משנה does not contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: His normal way; what he usually does

phrases.english: רבא can say to you:
What does 'he gave it to a shepherd' mean? To his helper,
phrases.notes: The shepherd here is the one who got the animal, and he passed it on to his own assistant.

phrases.english: for it is a shepherd's normal way to hand over to his helper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by narrowing the case in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the משנה describes a shepherd passing the animal to his assistant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to let any שומר pass the animal to any other שומר and walk away free.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only covers a shepherd giving the animal to his own helper, which is expected. רבא's rule about outside שומרים still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule holds: handing to an outside שומר keeps you liable. A shepherd passing the animal to his helper is a normal, expected exception.

steps.title: Second version: the משנה's wording shows it means the helper
steps.stepSummary: Some say the same idea comes straight from the משנה's wording. It says 'to a shepherd,' not 'to another,' so it must mean the shepherd's helper, and handing to an outsider would not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: since the משנה says 'he gave it to a shepherd' and not 'he gave it to another,' learn from it that it means the shepherd gave it to his helper, since that is a shepherd's normal way. But to another person, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the discussion. Here the same point is read from the משנה's choice of words, not raised as a defense. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version nobody attacks רבא first. The exact word 'shepherd' is treated as a clue that the משנה only allows the normal handoff to a helper. Handing to an outsider is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say; introduces a second version of the discussion
Learn from it; we can conclude from this

phrases.english: Some say:
Since the משנה teaches 'he gave it to a shepherd'
and does not teach 'he gave it to another,'
learn from it: what does 'he gave it to a shepherd' mean?
The shepherd gave it to his helper,
for it is a shepherd's normal way to hand over to his helper;
but to another person, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the point of step 11 as an inference from the משנה's wording, in a second version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the משנה says 'shepherd' and not 'another,' it covers only a shepherd passing the animal to his helper, not to an outsider.

steps.title: Does this wording prove רבא right?
steps.stepSummary: Based on that reading, the גמרא suggests the משנה actually supports רבא's rule that handing over to another שומר keeps you liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports רבא, who said: a guardian who handed over to another guardian is liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to turn the wording from step 12 into a proof for רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה deliberately excludes handing to an outsider, it fits רבא's view that such a handoff leaves the first שומר liable. In the first version the משנה was a problem for רבא; in this version it would be support.

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports רבא?
For רבא said:
A guardian who handed over to another guardian is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 12's reading to suggest a proof for רבא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that a שומר who hands over to another שומר is liable
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's choice of 'to a shepherd' over 'to another,' which seems to exclude handing to an outsider

steps.title: No proof: the משנה may just describe the usual case
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The משנה may say 'shepherd' only because that is what usually happens, and the law might be the same for anyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: No. Perhaps it teaches the usual way things happen, and the same is true for another person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof for רבא from step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Choosing the word 'shepherd' may not be a deliberate limit. Animals are usually handed to shepherds, so the משנה just describes the common case. The law could be the same for an outsider, so the wording proves nothing for רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The usual way things happen; the common case

phrases.english: They say: No;
perhaps it teaches the usual way things happen,
and the same is true for another person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: לָא; דִּלְמָא אוֹרְחָא דְמִילְּתָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof suggested in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה's wording. It does not reject רבא's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'shepherd' may just describe the common case, not limit the law, so no inference can be drawn.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה neither disproves nor proves רבא. In the first version רבא explains it away; in the second version it fails to support him.
steps.confusionAlert: Rejecting the proof does not mean רבא is wrong. It only means this משנה cannot be used as evidence for him.

steps.title: The dispute about someone guarding a lost item
steps.stepSummary: רבה says a שומר אבידה is like a שומר חנם. רב יוסף says he is like a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: what about a person who is guarding a lost item? רבה said: he is like an unpaid guard. רב יוסף said: he is like a paid guard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It brings a disagreement about how responsible a finder is while he holds a lost item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר חנם pays only if he was careless. A שומר שכר also pays if the item is stolen or lost. So the question is how much the finder must pay if something happens to the item while he holds it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated; this introduces a disagreement between אמוראים
Someone guarding a lost item he found, until he returns it
Unpaid guard; he pays only if he was careless
Paid guard; he also pays if the item is stolen or lost

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבה here with רבא from the earlier steps. They are two different אמוראים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic level of responsibility for anyone who keeps a lost item for its owner.

phrases.english: It was stated: one who guards a lost item —
Rabba said: he is like an unpaid guard,

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: כְּשׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: he is like a paid guard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the shepherd and רבא's rule ended in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה: a שומר אבידה is a שומר חנם. רב יוסף: a שומר אבידה is a שומר שכר.

steps.title: The reasons behind each side
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the finder gets no benefit. רב יוסף says he does get a benefit, because he does not have to give bread to a poor person while he is busy with this מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said he is like an unpaid guard, because what benefit does he get? רב יוסף said he is like a paid guard, because of the benefit that he does not have to give bread to a poor person. So he counts as a paid guard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind each opinion from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that a שומר שכר is someone who gets a benefit. They argue about whether the finder gets one. רב יוסף points to a small benefit: while he is busy with this מצוה, he does not have to give charity to a poor person who asks. That small gain is enough to make him a paid guard.

phrases.english: Rabba said he is like an unpaid guard —
what benefit does he get from it?

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר כְּשׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר דָּמֵי –
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said he is like a paid guard —
because of that benefit, that he does not need
to give bread to a poor person,
phrases.notes: The idea is that while you are busy with one מצוה, like caring for the lost item, you don't have to do another one.

phrases.english: he is like a paid guard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the two opinions given in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Getting a benefit is what makes someone a שומר שכר. רבה sees no benefit here. רב יוסף sees a benefit in being free from giving charity at that time.

steps.title: A second way to explain רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: Some explain רב יוסף differently: since the תורה forces him to guard the item against his will, it treats him like a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some explain it this way: רב יוסף said he is like a paid guard because the Merciful One obligated him against his will. Therefore he is like a paid guard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different explanation of why רב יוסף says the finder is a שומר שכר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explanation does not depend on any benefit at all. The reason is that the תורה itself put the job on him, even though he did not choose it. So the תורה holds him to the stricter standard of a paid guard.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Obligated him, put the duty on him

steps.whatToRemember: רבה: a finder is a שומר חנם because he gets no benefit. רב יוסף: a finder is a שומר שכר, either because he is free from giving charity while busy, or because the תורה forces the job on him.

phrases.english: There are those who explain it like this:

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר כְּשׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר דָּמֵי –
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said he is like a paid guard —
since the Merciful One obligated him against his will,
therefore he is like a paid guard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reason for רב יוסף instead of the benefit reason in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A duty the תורה forces on someone makes him as responsible as a שומר שכר.

steps.title: A memory list for the coming discussions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a list of keywords to help remember the challenges and rulings that come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: A memory aid: he returned it, always, return, חייא, you said, broke, payment.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא lists keywords so the learner can remember the order of the discussions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new law is taught here. Each word is a hint to a later passage that tests the dispute between רבה and רב יוסף. You will see these words come up one at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: Memory aid, a list of keywords

phrases.english: (Memory aid: he returned it, always,
return, Chiyya, you said,
broke, payment.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Prepares for the series of challenges to the רבה and רב יוסף dispute that follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. It is a memory aid for the passages that follow.

steps.title: רב יוסף gets ready to challenge רבה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף announces that he is bringing a challenge against רבה's view that a שומר אבידה is like a שומר חנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף brought a challenge against רבה from a teaching:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. רב יוסף is about to quote a source that seems to argue against רבה, but the source itself has not been quoted yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in Step 15, רבה said a finder is like a שומר חנם and רב יוסף said he is like a שומר שכר. Now רב יוסף tries to prove his side by attacking רבה from an earlier source. The word אֵיתִיבֵיהּ tells us a challenge from a written source is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (by quoting an older source, like a משנה or ברייתא)
The אמורא who holds that a finder is like a paid guard
The אמורא who holds that a finder is like an unpaid guard

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as a question that wants information. אֵיתִיבֵיהּ always starts an attack from an older source, and the source itself comes right after.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection to Rabba:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the memory keywords in Step 18, the גמרא starts the first challenge in the list. It goes back to the argument between רבה and רב יוסף from Steps 15-17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that a שומר אבידה is like a שומר חנם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יוסף will quote an older teaching that seems to give the finder the stricter responsibility of a paid guard. That would go against רבה. The teaching itself comes on the next amud.
